RETRACTION FIRST, then two live findings. That was WRONG and the block is RIGHT: 'the substrate variable' here is the LADDER variable u = b*hbar_q^2, not q_0. Recomputed from the sibling radius-of-convergence gate's own table, u(proton) = 0.008517234550156142 and u(muon) = 0.008517236340043958, a relative shift of 2.10149e-7 = 210.15 ppb -- exactly as printed. The 18.2x amplification from q to u is real and derivable: d(ln u)/d(ln q) = 2/(q*hbar_q) = 18.19, because hbar_q = 1 - 1/q is small and enters squared. The surviving point is only that 'the substrate variable' reads naturally as q_0 (which the corpus calls the substrate parameter) and that 210 ppb happens to coincide with the m_mu prediction error, so the phrase invites exactly the misreading I made; proposed clarification: 'the ladder variable u shifts by 2.1e-7'.
